instructions: Open a new setup chat from current environment settings. Read its current draft and reconcile this proposal before saving. Preserve all existing presets, domains, bindings, and repository membership. Do not treat this file as an active configuration.

config.install_script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /workspace/Sona
export XDG_DATA_HOME=/workspace/.local/share
if [ "$(node --version)" != "v24.19.0" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'Sona requires Node 24.19.0.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ "$(pnpm --version)" != "11.19.0" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'Sona requires pnpm 11.19.0.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm check
pnpm test
pnpm build
config.start_skill:
# Sona cloud workspace

Work in /workspace/Sona. Read docs/implementation/execution-log.md and applicable AGENTS.md before changes. Product authority is docs/prd/Sona-PRD.md, version 1.0, with docs/implementation/workspace-refinement.md for the user's later changes. Use the existing checkout. Do not create a Git worktree unless the user explicitly requests one.

Node 24.19.0 and pnpm 11.19.0 are pinned. Export XDG_DATA_HOME=/workspace/.local/share for installation and all pnpm commands. Use CI=true for frozen-lockfile installation. Use pnpm's default store with that XDG path. Keep application data outside /workspace/Sona.

After setup, run pnpm start for the built application on local port 4317. Keep it in a managed terminal. Check /api/health and /api/bootstrap at http://127.0.0.1:4317. Do not print the bootstrap token. Stop the process with Ctrl+C or signal only its owned process.

For development, run pnpm dev. The browser origin is http://127.0.0.1:5173. Optional SONA_PORT and SONA_WEB_PORT select local ports; the browser proxy and development Origin allowlist use those selections. Keep SONA_DATA_DIR outside the checkout.

Run pnpm check, pnpm test, pnpm build, and pnpm test:e2e after relevant source changes. Linux browser tests use /usr/bin/chromium. Set SONA_CHROMIUM_PATH only when a different installed Chromium executable is necessary. API coverage is pnpm coverage:api. Packaging is pnpm package. The extracted-release check is pnpm verify:release.

No credential is necessary for local catalog, configuration, unit, or synthetic browser checks. For live voice, open Sona Settings and enter a project API key. It stays in local server memory until restart. Saving does not verify provider access. Live voice also needs authorized model access. Google MCP needs Sona's own supported authorization and dedicated test resource. Optional admin and webhook operations use separate OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY and OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Use GUI entry for the normal project key. Optional legacy CLI, independent runtime, admin, webhook, and Google credentials use private server bindings. Do not assume this coding session's connectors transfer to Sona.

The live prerequisite command is pnpm test:live. SONA_LIVE=1 adds local runtime checks. Exit code 2 means blocked verification. It does not open paid calls or perform external writes. Follow docs/verification/live-checks.md for real voice, Calendar, device, account, and teammate checks. Keep the bounded admission budget and dedicated test resources. Do not publish or deploy.

Future real-service work needs permitted outbound access to api.openai.com, calendarmcp.googleapis.com, accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, and openidconnect.googleapis.com. Official source and price review needs raw.githubusercontent.com, developers.openai.com, and openai.com. Actual GitHub repository API requests and pull-request creation now succeed. api.github.com is necessary for that workflow. A saved draft alone does not prove runtime access. Preserve existing presets and other settings. Do not bypass the proxy or branch protections.

Use the supplied ASD-STE100 Issue 9 for technical writing when available. Do not run the archived language checker or generate a compliance score.
